about: Every number on these slides and in their speaker notes, with its source. All of them come from synthetic tasks.

claims.number: 31 seed packs in one library, with 556 nouns and 182 verb templates
claims.source: A count of the packs in the seed-pack library on October 30, 2026. They are proposals and validated examples: none is installed, imported, admitted or activated.
A continuous tuning loop built from nouns and verbs on one local GPU, October 29, 2026, scored on a frozen, synthetic tool-call test of 150 rows.
The same loop and the same frozen, synthetic test, October 29, 2026.

claims.number: Muse Glimmer 30B: exact match 93.3% to 99.3%, +6.0 points, 95% CI +2.0 to +10.7; promotion rule 12 of 12
claims.source: QLoRA on free cloud GPUs for the same kind of synthetic task, scored on a fresh 150-row test whose hashes were registered before scoring. A fresh reload reproduced its outputs. The rule said promote; nothing has been promoted or admitted. The run record, with every file's hash, is published with this deck's evidence.

claims.number: 10/10 agent processes finished their shared tasks in one wave
claims.source: Ten native Pi processes on synthetic tasks, October 29, 2026. Earlier waves of 7/10 and 3/3 are also on record.

claims.number: 100/100 protocol clients in 25.7 seconds, with no rate-limit rejections
claims.source: A short protocol load test on October 29, 2026: 25.663 seconds and no HTTP 429. Expected write conflicts did occur. Not 100 separate agent programs.

claims.number: 6 agent programs each finished a scoped task; 6 of 14 attempts passed
claims.source: OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Muse Code, nanoMuse and OpenClaw in narrow lifecycle tests, with every failure recorded. A seventh program, Claude Code, passed a separate test later.

claims.number: 0 model tokens while compiled code recipes run
claims.source: Compiled recipes run as plain code; six local deterministic runs are recorded. Making or checking a recipe can still use a model.
